module purpose: neorv32_cpu is a top-level CPU wrapper that connects frontend, control, counters, register-file, ALU, load/store, optional PMP and optional ICC subunits. It forwards external interrupts and bus/ICC interfaces, computes the machine-interrupt bundle, aggregates extension CSR data, and combines execution, load/store, CSR and pc-return results into the register-file write-back bus.

use-case flows.value: debug request delivered to the CPU control block
fast interrupt request vector delivered to the CPU control block
three-bit machine interrupt request vector assembled from mti_i, mei_i and msi_i and delivered to the CPU control block
extension CSR read data combined from counters, ALU, PMP and ICC sources and delivered to the control block
register-file write-back bus formed from execution, load/store, CSR and pc-return sources and sent to the register file
PMP fault/no-fault indication produced by the optional PMP block, sent to control and LSU, or forced low when PMP is disabled

conceptual assets.concept: Debug request event entering CPU control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow passes dbi_i directly into the control sub-unit at line 266. The module's control behavior therefore depends on the consumer receiving exactly this request value; under the cross-boundary integrity rule, corrupting that delivered event would make debug-entry handling incorrect. Availability is also established only as delivery of the asserted request to the consumer.

conceptual assets.concept: Fast interrupt request vector entering CPU control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow passes firq_i directly into the control sub-unit at line 268. The control logic depends on receiving the exact vector presented at this port, so integrity of the delivered request is established by the RTL-to-consumer connection. Availability is also established as presentation of the vector to the consumer.

conceptual assets.concept: Machine interrupt request vector delivered to CPU control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow explicitly computes `irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i;` at line 276 and sends that vector to control at line 267. Integrity requires the three-bit value consumed by control to match the concatenation defined in line 276; otherwise interrupt qualification inside the consumer becomes incorrect. Availability is established as combinational production and delivery of that vector.

The read-out flow computes `xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc;` at line 279 and delivers it to control as `xcsr_rdata_i` at line 264. The contributing terms come from sub-units or are forced to zero when disabled: counters at line 299 or line 305, PMP at line 416 or line 426, ICC at line 445 or line 454, and ALU at line 371. Integrity is established because CSR handling in the consumer depends on receiving exactly the aggregate defined by line 279 for the enabled-feature build. Availability is also established because disabled contributors are explicitly driven to zero and enabled contributors are wired into the aggregate.

The operate flow computes `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;` at line 330 and sends that value to the register-file sub-unit as `rd_i` at line 323. Integrity is established because the register-file consumer must receive exactly the write-back bus value defined by line 330; corrupting it would make architectural state updates incorrect. Availability is also established as continuous formation of this bus from its contributors for any write-back that the regfile performs.

When `RISCV_ISA_Smpmp` is enabled, the report flow takes `fault_o` from the PMP sub-unit into `pmp_fault` at line 420 and delivers that decision to control and LSU at lines 257 and 392. When the feature is disabled, line 427 forces `pmp_fault <= '0'`. Integrity is established because access-handling behavior in those consumers depends on receiving the exact enabled-build fault indication, or the exact forced-low value in the disabled build. Availability is established under the applicable configuration by either the PMP connection or the explicit constant drive.
